phase_name: Publication Chapter Retrospective, System Execution Readiness Assessment, and PCAE Roadmap Re-Baseline
summary: Independently retrospected all seven Publication-chapter phases (144A-144G), confirming the strict Architecture -> Contract Freeze -> Implementation -> Verification -> Contract Revision -> Implementation -> Verification alternation and that only Phase 144C and Phase 144F touched src/. Independently re-read all seven phase documents directly, not any phase's own self-summary, and confirmed: 144A's ownership-model selection (dedicated PublicationCoordinator); 144B's PEC-001 v1.0 freeze (110 requirements, 9 adversarial scenarios resolved); 144C's first real implementation (src/pcae/governance/publication/**) and its own disclosed-but-unclassified JC-2 gap; 144D's independent escalation of JC-2 into finding F-1 (classified Blocking-for-future-production-use); 144E's contract revision (IWC-001 v1.1->v1.2 Sec.26, PEC-001 v1.0->v1.1 Sec.20) closing the gap at the contract level only; 144F's implementation widening Session/Preview/PublicationReadinessPackage/record.py, discovering the gap was one layer deeper than 144E assumed (four of nine IWC-REQ-185 fields never captured upstream at all, not merely dropped at Package construction); and 144G's independent re-verification finding zero Blocking findings while directly cross-checking record.py's output against human_governance_record.schema.json and finding it missing 14 of 19 required fields (Non-Blocking/Deferred, consistent with PEC-001's own literal text). Produced a capability inventory across twelve subsystems (Runtime, Lifecycle, Interactive Workflow, Typed Authority Model, Repository Intelligence, Publication, Governance, Canonical Reports, Notification, Historical Memory, Dependency Knowledge, Permission Broker), explicitly distinguishing subsystems independently re-verified this phase by direct reading of their governing phase documents (Publication, Interactive Workflow via Phase 143P's own end-to-end certification, Typed Authority Model via Phase 136AW/137G/137N, Advisory Governance via Phase 141G) from those assessed only via pcae architecture-status inspect's completed-phase index and live command output (Repository Intelligence, Historical Memory, Dependency Knowledge, Notification, and Canonical Lifecycle State Authority beyond Phase 135A) -- disclosed explicitly as this assessment's own research gap, not overclaimed. Walked the full user-request-to-canonical-publication execution chain across ten stages and found governed decision-making (Interactive Workflow, Publication) architecture-complete and independently verified but unreachable by any CLI/transport surface, independently confirmed via a fresh grep -rn "interactive_workflow" src/pcae/cli.py returning zero matches, while Runtime execution and Permission Broker enforcement remain unimplemented, independently confirmed via pcae runtime inspect returning Runtime status: not_implemented, Permission Broker status: execution_unavailable, Registry status: empty, Plugin count: 0. Independently discovered and documented a three-way roadmap-tracking disagreement: pcae roadmap current reports phase 69P, docs/ROADMAP.md reports 90B, and the actual repository state (git log, pcae architecture-status inspect) is 144G/144H -- classified as governance debt. Concluded, with evidence, that the original v0.2 107-115 execution-capability roadmap sequence (docs/V0_2_AUTONOMY_ROADMAP.md, Phase 107A) should be re-baselined rather than literally resumed, since Interactive Workflow, the Typed Authority Model, and Publication did not exist when Phase 107A's own gap analysis was written. Ranked future chapters by architectural necessity: an Interactive Workflow + Publication CLI/transport phase ranked highest (lowest risk, would unlock roughly thirty already-verified but currently unreachable chapters of prior work), ahead of Runtime/Permission Broker implementation itself, which remains the largest true gap but carries higher risk and no readiness finding in this phase's own research changed that. Assessment only; no governance, lifecycle, contract, or production-code change; explicit no-go confirmed. Runtime confirmed unchanged (Observed/observe/unavailable) via pcae runtime inspect at phase start and close. This phase's recommendation does not authorize any later phase. See docs/PHASE_144H_PUBLICATION_CHAPTER_RETROSPECTIVE_SYSTEM_EXECUTION_READINESS_ASSESSMENT_AND_ROADMAP_REBASELINE.md.
